proposal.utterance: Classify 'Abusus' (the right of abuse, in Roman-law property theory) in BFO terms.

entities.label: Abusus
entities.rationale: Abusus (ius abutendi) is the right of abuse or alienation in Roman property theory — one of the three classical sticks in the dominium bundle (usus, fructus, abusus). It is a socially and legally conferred entitlement that inheres in a person qua owner within a legal system; it is externally grounded in the legal-institutional structure rather than in the intrinsic constitution of the bearer. This makes it a Role (BFO_0000023), specifically a kind of LegalRight (already in the ontology as a subclass of BFO_0000023). It is modelled as a class rather than an individual because 'Abusus' denotes a kind of right that any owner could bear, not a specific token right.

relations.rationale: Abusus is a species of LegalRight: it is one of the three analytically distinguishable entitlements comprising full dominium in Roman property theory. Subclassing under LegalRight (itself a subclass of BFO_0000023 Role) preserves the bundle-of-rights structure.

open_questions: Should the classical Roman-law bundle be modelled as a whole (dominium) with Abusus, Usus, and Fructus as named parts? If so, shall we also mint Usus and Fructus as sibling classes of Abusus under LegalRight?
Is the intent to model Abusus as a generic Roman-law concept (class), or are we analysing a specific token right borne by a particular owner in a particular transaction (individual)?

Should we distinguish Abusus-as-power-to-alienate (a Hohfeldian power/role) from Abusus-as-liberty-to-destroy (a Hohfeldian privilege)? This could affect whether some aspects are better typed as Disposition (BFO_0000016) rather than Role.

Is there an intent to connect Abusus to a broader dominium class, or to a specific legal system (e.g., Roman law, civil-law jurisdictions) via a NormValidationCriteria or LegalArchitecture individual?
proposal.rationale_summary: Abusus — the ius abutendi of Roman dominium — is the legally conferred entitlement of an owner to alienate, consume, or destroy the thing owned. In BFO terms it is best classified as a Role (BFO_0000023): it is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a person (or legal person) bearing the status of owner, and it is externally grounded in the institutional-legal structure rather than in the bearer's intrinsic properties. The existing working class LegalRight (already typed as BFO_0000023) is the natural parent, because Abusus is one species in the classical Roman tripartite decomposition of dominium (usus, fructus, abusus). It is introduced as a class rather than an individual because it denotes a kind of right rather than a particular token right-instance. No individual is minted at this stage. Open questions concern whether sibling classes (Usus, Fructus) and a parent Dominium class should also be introduced, and whether the Hohfeldian power/liberty ambiguity warrants a finer-grained typing.
